rows.selection_reason: 1) Evidence/uncertainty: No experiments have been completed, so there is zero information about how any modality, encoder, or fusion strategy performs. The most fundamental uncertainty is the baseline performance of the simplest RNA-only pipeline. 2) What this tests: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) establishes the most basic reference point—a single-profile RNA model with a standard linear encoder (PCA). It isolates the RNA signal quality and the single-profile assumption without confounding from image data, complex encoders, or aggregation. 3) Why it is the best first experiment: It is the simplest, fastest-running configuration in the space, minimizing risk of a failed or noisy first result. It provides the anchor against which all image-only, multimodal, multiprofile, and alternative-encoder experiments can be compared. Establishing this baseline first ensures that subsequent experiments (e.g., adding image, switching to multiprofile, or trying scGPT/SCVI) can be interpreted as marginal gains over a well-defined reference, making the limited budget maximally informative.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only/singleprofile/pca_n2000 at ~48.5% acc), the dominant uncertainty is whether the image modality carries meaningful signal for this task. config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cleanest test of this question: it matches config_001 on profile setting (singleprofile) and uses a standard, well-calibrated image encoder, so the primary variable is modality itself. If image-only substantially outperforms RNA-only, the search should pivot toward image encoders and multimodal fusion; if it performs similarly or worse, RNA remains the primary signal and we should explore RNA encoders and multiprofile aggregation. Resolving this structural question first maximizes information gain per experiment and prevents wasting budget on secondary design choices (aggregation, fusion strategy, encoder variants) before knowing which modality is most informative.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA (config_001) achieves 48.5% accuracy, far outperforming image-only ResNet50 (config_010, 20.8%), establishing RNA as the dominant modality. However, we only have one RNA data point and no information on whether multiprofile aggregation adds value. Question: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) directly extends config_001 by changing only the profile setting from single to multi and adding avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of multi-profile aggregation while keeping the encoder fixed. Why this is best: With only 2 experiments completed, the highest-value uncertainty to reduce is whether the structural choice of multiprofile vs. singleprofile matters for our strongest modality. This is a minimal, confound-free extension of our best result. If multiprofile helps, it validates investing in the broader multiprofile space (including multimodal); if not, it saves budget by narrowing the search. Testing a new encoder (scVI/scGPT) or jumping to multimodal fusion would introduce multiple simultaneous changes and make attribution harder at this early stage.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) achieves 0.591 acc, substantially better than singleprofile (0.485), confirming multiprofile + aggregation is the strongest direction so far. However, we have no evidence about whether the aggregation method itself matters—avgpool is the simplest option. Question: config_003 is identical to config_002 except it replaces avgpool with a transformer aggregator, giving a clean single-variable test of whether learned attention-based profile combination captures interactions that simple averaging misses. Why this is the best next experiment: it directly extends our strongest result with a minimal, interpretable change; the outcome (transformer >> avgpool, ≈, or <<) will determine the aggregation architecture for all subsequent multimodal experiments, making it high-information per budget unit. It also avoids the risk of confounding encoder choice (scvi/scgpt) with aggregation choice in a single step.

Evidence: RNA-only with multi-profile + avgpool + PCA (config_002, acc=0.591) is the clear best configuration so far, while image-only with ResNet50 single-profile (config_010, acc=0.208) is very weak. The core question for this multimodal study is whether combining the two modalities yields a benefit over the RNA-only baseline. config_018 (multimodal, multi-profile, PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) directly tests this by pairing the best-known RNA setup with the only image encoder already characterized, using the simplest fusion strategy. If accuracy exceeds 0.591, image contributes complementary signal and justifies exploring better image encoders and fusion strategies; if it falls below, image is currently harmful and the budget should shift toward RNA encoder improvements (scvi, scgpt) or stronger image backbones. This is the highest-information experiment because its outcome determines the entire direction of subsequent experiments in a multimodal study.

Evidence: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA-2000, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) is our best result at 0.619 acc / 0.610 F1, showing that multimodal fusion with avgpool aggregation provides a ~2.8% boost over the best RNA-only config (config_002, 0.591). However, we have only tested concat fusion; the effect of weighted fusion is completely untested. Question: config_019 is an exact single-variable ablation of config_018, changing only fusion from concat to weighted. This directly tests whether a learned weighting of modalities outperforms simple concatenation, which is a critical design decision for any multimodal system. Why this is the best next experiment: (1) It is the cleanest possible A/B comparison against our current best, isolating one variable; (2) fusion strategy is a high-leverage design choice that, if improved, benefits all future multimodal configurations; (3) it is low-risk and immediately actionable — a positive result gives a free upgrade to our best config, while a negative result confirms concat is sufficient and redirects budget toward other axes (RNA encoder, image encoder); (4) under a limited budget, resolving this binary question before exploring higher-dimensional changes (new encoders) avoids confounding multiple untested factors simultaneously.

Evidence: The current best (config_019: multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.639) shows that multimodal fusion with weighted combination and avgpool aggregation is the strongest configuration. However, the image modality is very weak in isolation (config_010: resnet50 singleprofile, acc=0.208), raising the question of whether a stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) could contribute more informative features to the fusion. This experiment (config_025) is a clean single-variable extension of config_019, changing only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while keeping all validated settings (multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion, pca_n2000). It directly tests whether the image branch is a bottleneck and whether upgrading it yields meaningful multimodal gains. Under a limited budget, this is the highest-information experiment: it either confirms that the current resnet50 features are sufficient (allowing us to focus on RNA encoder improvements) or reveals that a stronger visual backbone unlocks substantially better multimodal performance, guiding all subsequent experiments.

Evidence: The current best configuration (config_019, acc=0.639) uses pca_n2000 as the RNA encoder with multimodal fusion (resnet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile). All completed experiments have used pca_n2000; the RNA encoder dimension is completely unexplored. The image modality contributes only modestly over RNA-only (0.639 vs 0.591), suggesting the RNA representation quality is the primary performance driver. Question tested: Does a learned single-cell latent representation (scvi_n200) outperform a linear PCA projection in the best multimodal setup? This is a clean single-variable change from config_019. Why this is the best next experiment: The RNA encoder is the largest untested design axis with potentially high impact. Resolving whether a nonlinear learned encoder helps (or hurts) in the multimodal context will either open a new improvement direction or confirm PCA sufficiency, thereby reducing the effective search space for all subsequent experiments. It is more informative than re-testing aggregation (avgpool already has strong RNA-only evidence) or image encoder (resnet50 vs ViT-L showed negligible difference).

The strongest evidence so far identifies scvi_n200 + resnet50 + avgpool + weighted (config_031, 0.678 acc) as the best configuration, with scvi_n200 providing a large jump over pca_n2000 (+3.9%). The remaining uncertainty is whether a stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l vs resnet50) could further complement the scvi_n200 representation—the prior evidence is weak (only 0.4% difference with pca_n2000, config_019 vs config_025). config_037 isolates this single variable (image encoder) while holding all other proven-optimal settings fixed (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion). This is the best use of the next budget slot because it exploits the strongest known direction while resolving a genuinely uncertain design choice; a positive result would immediately identify a new best configuration, and a null/negative result would confirm resnet50 suffices, freeing subsequent experiments to explore other axes (e.g., scgpt encoder or transformer aggregation).

The RNA encoder has proven to be the most impactful design choice: switching from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 yielded +0.071 accuracy in the multimodal/vit_l setting (0.635→0.706). However, scgpt is completely untested across all experiments, leaving significant uncertainty about whether it could outperform scvi_n200. Config_049 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, vit_l, avgpool, weighted) changes only the RNA encoder from the current best config (037), making it a clean single-variable test. If scgpt matches or exceeds scvi, it opens a new promising direction; if it falls short, it confirms scvi as the superior encoder and lets us focus remaining budget on aggregation or fusion refinements. This is the highest-information experiment available because it resolves the largest remaining uncertainty (encoder choice) in the context of the best-performing configuration.
